title: Learning Human Health and Diseases from 24-hour Wrist Movement
abstract: arXiv:2608.29494v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Much of human health and function unfolds beyond the clinic, through the movements of everyday life. Wrist-worn accelerometers capture these movements continuously, yet their rich signals are often reduced to a small set of predefined behavioural summary measures. Here, we present Sensori, a self-supervised foundation model that learns general-purpose health representations directly from 24 hours of raw tri-axial wrist movement. We developed and evaluated the model across four population-based cohorts from the United Kingdom, China and the United States, comprising 122,640 participants contributing 683,617 person-days of free-living recordings. Sensori condensed each day of movement into a representation that captured diverse movement behaviours, demographic characteristics, health axes and physical function. translated_title: 从24小时腕部运动中学习人类健康与疾病
translated_abstract: 人类的健康与功能很大程度上在临床之外展开，体现在日常生活的运动之中。腕戴式加速度计可以连续捕捉这些运动，但其丰富的信号通常被简化为少量预定义的行为汇总指标。在此，我们提出了Sensori，一个自监督基础模型，可直接从24小时的原始三轴腕部运动中学习通用的健康表征。我们在来自英国、中国和美国的四个基于人群的队列中开发并评估了该模型，涵盖122,640名参与者，共贡献683,617人日的自由生活记录。Sensori将每天的运动压缩为一种表征，该表征捕获了多样的运动行为、人口统计学特征、健康维度和身体功能。在独立队列中的评估表明，这些表征能够在不同人群和测量环境下实现泛化。
tldr: 本文提出了自监督基础模型Sensori，可直接从24小时原始腕部运动数据中学习通用健康表征，并在英、中、美四个人群队列共12万余名参与者的数据上验证了其在捕获运动行为、健康指标和身体功能方面的跨人群泛化能力。
en_tdlr: Sensori, a self-supervised foundation model, learns general-purpose health representations directly from 24-hour raw tri-axial wrist movement, demonstrating generalization across four population-based cohorts totaling over 122,000 participants in the UK, China, and the US.
